harvestProduct: fruit; keep whole fruit and processed portions separate

evidence.quote: Can vary tremendously, but a cycle time of 18 months is normal at Hluhluwe.
evidence.doc: KZN DARD, Fruit and Nut Production in KZN (2006), Pineapple: Bearing Age

yearsToFirstCrop.notes: Hluhluwe production-cycle reference: 18 months / 12 = 1.5 years. The source explicitly says cycle length varies greatly. Starting material, cultivar, weather and flower initiation matter; this is neither a universal first-harvest date nor a 12-month annual yield.

yearsToFullBearing.notes: No species-wide full-bearing age stated. Pineapple is a plant/ratoon crop, not an orchard tree; Queen plantings in this guide are re-established after the plant crop.

yieldKgPerTreeMature.notes: The source supplies hectare crop-cycle yields and distinct cultivar planting densities. It does not attribute each yield class to a cultivar/density or supply an annual age-yield curve. Keep these native references separate rather than multiply a mapped plant by an invented annual kg default.

chillUnits.notes: No numeric chilling requirement. The guide identifies frost and cold as production hazards.

pollination.notes: No species-wide pollination requirement stated in this regional production guide.

productionGuidance.products: Pineapple fruit; whole fruit and processed portions have different weights.
care: Use a warm, frost-free, well-drained site. The KZN production reference is Hluhluwe; it does not establish suitability throughout South Africa.
Record planting and actual picking dates. Year-round commercial planting or marketing does not mean every planted pineapple gives fruit in every month.
purchase: KZN guide: Queen is a fresh-fruit candidate; Smooth Cayenne is mainly a processing candidate. Confirm clean crowns/suckers, local suitability and crop-cycle advice with a nursery. Queen re-establishment after the plant crop belongs in the future plan.

supplementaryReferences.title: Hluhluwe crop-cycle output
supplementaryReferences.doc: KZN DARD, Fruit and Nut Production in KZN (2006), Pineapple
supplementaryReferences.note: Regional hectare reference: conservative 50 t/ha, average 60–75 t/ha, good 80 t/ha per production crop. The same page describes a normal 18-month Hluhluwe cycle. These are not kg/plant/year or a forecast for a household planting.

supplementaryReferences.title: Cultivar and renewal choice
supplementaryReferences.quote: Queen – Suckers planted at 120 000 to 150 000 plants per hectare tend to give optimum yields, but need to be re-established after the plant crop. ... Smooth Cayenne - mainly processing, weight 2kg ... Queen - mainly fresh market, weight 0.75kg
supplementaryReferences.doc: KZN DARD, Fruit and Nut Production in KZN (2006), Pineapple: Spacing and Cultivars
supplementaryReferences.note: Queen and Smooth Cayenne serve different uses. The guide's example fruit weights (Queen 0.75 kg; Smooth Cayenne 2 kg) are cultivar descriptions, not annual yields per plant. Queen is re-established after the plant crop in this system.

supplementaryReferences.title: Climate and calendar conditions
supplementaryReferences.quote: Plants are frost sensitive. ... Good drainage is essential ... In the warmer production area of Hluhluwe there is year-round planting. In cooler areas planting is restricted to the warmer months
supplementaryReferences.doc: KZN DARD, Fruit and Nut Production in KZN (2006), Pineapple: Climate and Planting Times
supplementaryReferences.note: Frost sensitivity and drainage constrain the site. Year-round planting at Hluhluwe is a planting reference, not an all-year household picking window; cooler sites use warmer planting months.

gaps: Checked 11 October 2026 against the official guide and rendered PDF page 22 (printed page 18). No fixed local picking-month array is stated. Chemical flower-initiation and commercial marketing references must not become a household all-year calendar.

No generic annual per-plant age-yield curve, full-bearing age or species-wide chill/pollination value is supplied by this source. Regional establishment and output references are retained and shown in their original units.
